facts.statement: Yantaloong was described by Zhang and colleagues.
Yantaloong lived during the Middle Jurassic period.
The type locality of Yantaloong is the Zhanghe Formation.
Yantaloong fossils were found in China.
If Yantaloong is classified as a turiasaur, it would be the first known turiasaur from East Asia.
facts.quote: If it is a turiasaur, it would be the first one known from East Asia.

facts.statement: The authors preferred a classification placing Yantaloong within Turiasauria based on an analysis showing the highest stability.
facts.quote: Zhang et al. preferred the turiasaurian placement derived from the equal weights analysis from the Moore et al. (2023) matrix, as these results demonstrate the highest stability

facts.statement: Some analyses suggest Yantaloong could be a non-neosauropod eusauropod outside traditional Turiasauria or a member of Neosauropoda, though these hypotheses are less favored.
Yantaloong exhibits a unique mix of derived traits found in dicraeosaurines and titanosaurs alongside primitive traits of basal eusauropods.
Yantaloong is likely the first discovered turiasaurian sauropod in China and East Asia.
